gcb-001.note: A bank reference letter in good order.

ug-001.note: A degree certificate. It has no validUntil.

emp-001.note: An employment letter in good order.

gcb-002.note: One letter of the account holder name was changed after signing.

gcb-003.note: Signed with a key that is not in the issuer DID document.

gcb-004.note: Its bit is set in the status list.

gcb-006.note: Signed with key-3 a month after key-3 was revoked.

gcb-007.note: Signed with key-1, which has since been retired in favour of key-2. Rotation does not disturb it.

gcb-008.note: Its status list is past its own validUntil, so revocation cannot be ruled out.

gcb-009.note: Carries a context that is not one of the two a claim may use.

gcb-010.note: Both revoked and past validUntil. Revocation is reported.

gcb-011.note: Signed with key-3 a month before key-3 was revoked.

gcb-012.note: A claim of one of the issuer's own types, version 1. Version 2 of the type exists; this claim is untouched by it.

gcb-013.note: The same type at version 2, with the field version 2 added.

gcb-014.note: An Attestation: the core type for a one-off statement.

gcb-015.note: A core type with an amount, which is a decimal string and never a number.

gcb-016.note: Correctly signed, but grade is not a value its schema allows. The answer is still valid; schemaValid reports the mismatch.

gcb-017.note: Every kind of field at once, so both languages canonicalise integers, booleans, dates and instants alike.

emp-002.note: A salary confirmation, a core type.

emp-003.note: Signed by one issuer against another issuer's type. An issuer may use core types and its own, nothing else.

ug-002.note: Its context is not bundled and is not in vectors/cache. Offline, nothing can be said about the signature.
